title: Mixtecan Family | SIL Mexico
text: The most famous collection of Mixtec artifacts was found in tomb seven at the Monte Alban archaeological site in Oaxaca. Like other Otomanguean languages, the languages in the Mixtecan family are tonal, which means that the pitch with which a word is pronounced is so important that a change in the pitch can change one word into an entirely different one.

title: Native American music - Mexico, Central America, Rituals | Britannica
text: November 20, 2007 - Part-singing and call and response continue to play a role in religious songs from Central Mexico, and instrumental ensembles employ chordal harmony. Dance music from this area features sectional forms with several short musical phrases in succession. The Mixtec perform certain song genres in their native languages, while other Central Mexican groups sing in Spanish.
